request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Instructions were missed.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A rule may help."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work\" prescribes no concrete behavior change, check, or decision rule that could alter what Claude does differently next time."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"This is pure platitude with no scope, mechanism, or condition — it is vague rather than usefully general, since it could apply to literally any failure and thus guides nothing."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"Not a skill, but even as a standing CLAUDE.md rule it has no defined trigger or scope — it's an always-on exhortation, which is the least targeted possible mechanism and will be lost among other instructions."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence details to leak."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"The failure statement is too underspecified to justify any specific remedy type, and adding a generic \"try harder\" line to global CLAUDE.md is not a cheap-and-adequate fix — it's a no-op that dilutes the instruction file without addressing whatever instruction was actually missed."}}

actionability.justification: "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work" prescribes no concrete behavior change, check, or decision rule that could alter what Claude does differently next time.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: This is pure platitude with no scope, mechanism, or condition — it is vague rather than usefully general, since it could apply to literally any failure and thus guides nothing.

leakage.justification: The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence details to leak.

routing_fitness.justification: The failure statement is too underspecified to justify any specific remedy type, and adding a generic "try harder" line to global CLAUDE.md is not a cheap-and-adequate fix — it's a no-op that dilutes the instruction file without addressing whatever instruction was actually missed.

trigger_quality.justification: Not a skill, but even as a standing CLAUDE.md rule it has no defined trigger or scope — it's an always-on exhortation, which is the least targeted possible mechanism and will be lost among other instructions.
